It is argued that by creating smaller terminal areas for the New Jersey forwarders, the Commission is placing them at a competitive disadvantage to the forwarders located in New York City. It is also argued that many operational inefficiencies would result. They urge that the proposed regulations be amended so that the terminal areas of freight forwarders located within 20 miles of New York City will be defined as coextensive with the New York, N.Y., commercial zone.
PRELIMINARY MATTERS
Several carriers contend that the complexity of the issues raised herein, as well as the gravity of impact upon the motor carrier industry entailed by expansion of commercial zones and terminal areas, merits a formal oral hearing, and that failure to provide for such oral participation is violative of procedural due process as guaranteed by the Constitution. They assert specifically that this Commission cannot fully consider the devastating effects of the proposed expansion upon smal! short-haul carriers without affording them an opportunity to appear and present oral evidence in this matter.
